lots.title: Stockport Town Centre School – Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment
lots.description: Briefing document (Document 7) issued by Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council for the appointment of a multi-disciplinary Design Team to deliver a new exemplar town centre through school on a brownfield site in Stockport town centre. The single-lot commission covers the full design workstream with an option to terminate or pause at each RIBA stage. RIBA Stage 2 funding has been secured from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. The brief describes context, ambition, opportunities and constraints, the disciplines required (Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, Building Regulations Principal Designer and CDM Principal Designer), the Competitive Flexible Procedure evaluation framework across Stage 1 (three equally-weighted questions) and Stage 2 (60% quality / 40% price / 20% social value), client team governance, and the indicative programme (PID 17/11/2025 → RIBA Stage 2 Cost Plan 31/08/2026). No additional internal lot structure is defined within this brief — it reinforces the single-lot Design Team appointment established by the notice (Contract Reference 020417).
requirements: Deliver a new exemplar town centre through school in central Stockport on a brownfield site, supporting the wider £1bn town centre regeneration programme.
Provide a multi-disciplinary Architecturally-led consultant team covering Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, Building Regulations Principal Designer (BR PD) and CDM Principal Designer (CDM PD).
Demonstrate prior experience of designing and delivering through schools of a similar size on complex, constrained and urban/town centre sites.
Design for inclusive education – facilities that meet the needs of all learners, with adaptable/flexible spaces that can evolve with changing educational needs.
Integrate the school with town centre regeneration, public realm and active travel, reducing reliance on cars and leveraging public transport accessibility.

Meet sustainability and future-proofing commitments: green building standards, active travel promotion, climate resilience (flood risk in response to the 2019 climate emergency declaration) and contribution to net zero targets.
Deliver Biodiversity Net Gain of 20% on the site.
Design with awareness of brownfield remediation complexity and high remediation costs.
Design around primary traffic routes that constrain the site and manage potential impact on environment and air quality.

Respond to governance arrangements: report to the SMBC Project Board (Estates, Education, MDC), Estates & Asset Management, Design & Technical Services, Education Services, Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation, local members, Local Planning Authority, Highways and Sustainability at agreed progress intervals; primary point of contact is the Head of Capital Design & Technical Services.

Deliver to the indicative RIBA programme: Submit PID 17/11/2025; Finalise Brief & prepare scope 12/01/2026 – 26/01/2026; Design Team appointment flow through RIBA Stage 2 design to Stage 2 Cost Plan by 31/08/2026 (with subsequent activity items through 29/06/2026, 20/07/2026, 27/07/2026 shown on the programme strip).
Provide consistency of team membership, especially at Partner level, across the design programme.
Develop and support a viable funding model for the Town Centre School project, integrating cost planning, risk management and lifecycle considerations with affordability.
